notes: Ensure that the self-healing logic is implemented in a way that it can be easily extended or modified in the future if needed.

steps.description: Identify the function responsible for executing shell commands in the executor
steps.details: Locate the function in the executor codebase that is responsible for executing shell commands. This function will be modified to include the self-healing logic.

steps.description: Modify the command execution function to detect missing dependencies
steps.details: Add logic to the command execution function to detect when a command fails due to a missing dependency. This can be done by checking the error message for common patterns indicating missing packages.

steps.description: Implement logic to install missing dependencies
steps.details: Within the command execution function, implement logic to parse the error message, extract the missing package name, and execute 'python -m pip install <package>'. Ensure this is done only once per command failure.

steps.description: Add retry logic for the failed command
steps.details: After attempting to install the missing dependency, retry the original command once. Ensure that if the command fails again, it does not enter an infinite loop.

steps.description: Implement error handling for failed installations
steps.details: Add error handling logic to provide a clear error message if the installation of the missing dependency fails. This message should indicate the failure and suggest possible manual resolution steps.

steps.description: Test the self-healing logic with various scenarios
steps.details: Create and run tests to ensure the self-healing logic works as expected. Test scenarios should include a missing dependency, successful installation, failed installation, and command retry behavior.
